title: I am, I don't etc.
subtitle: She isn't tired, but he is.
summary: Use a short form with am/is/have/do/can etc. so that you do not repeat the same words twice.

lesson.heading: Don't repeat the words
lesson.text: A woman says 'I'm not tired.' The man with her says 'I am.' This means *he is tired*. In the same way, a man says 'Yes, I do' when a woman asks 'Do you like tea?', and she says 'No, I don't.' He likes tea, but **she doesn't**. It is not necessary to repeat the words *tired* or *like tea*.

examples.note: she doesn't = she doesn't like tea

lesson.heading: Verbs you can use in this way
rows: I'm not married, but my brother **is**.
*A:* Are you tired? *B:* I **was**, but I'm not now.
I haven't got a car, but my sister **has**.
I don't like hot weather, but Sue **does**.
*A:* Please help me. *B:* I'm sorry. I **can't**.
Karen won't be here, but Chris **will**.
*A:* Do you think Jane will phone? *B:* She **might**.
*A:* Are you going now? *B:* Yes, I'm afraid I **must**.

lesson.heading: No short forms like 's or 've
lesson.text: You cannot end a sentence with **'m** / **'s** / **'ve**. You must use the full word **am**, **is**, **have** etc. But you *can* use the negative short forms **isn't**, **haven't**, **won't**.

examples.text: My sister has got a car, but I **haven't**.
*A:* Are you and Jane working tomorrow? *B:* I am, but Jane **isn't**.

lesson.heading: Yes and No answers
lesson.text: We use the same short forms after **Yes** and **No**. We do not repeat the whole sentence.

examples.text: *A:* Are you tired? *B:* Yes, **I am**. / No, **I'm not**.
*A:* Will Alan be here tomorrow? *B:* Yes, **he will**. / No, **he won't**.
*A:* Is there a bus to the airport? *B:* Yes, **there is**. / No, **there isn't**.

lesson.heading: do / does for the present
lesson.text: For the present simple (*like*, *work*, *watch* etc.) we use **do** and **does**.

examples.text: I don't like hot weather, but Sue **does**.
*A:* Do you enjoy your work? *B:* Yes, I **do**.

lesson.heading: did for the past
lesson.text: For the past simple (*enjoyed*, *had*, *rained* etc.) we use **did**.

examples.text: *A:* Did you and Chris enjoy the film? *B:* I **did**, but Chris **didn't**.
*A:* I had a good time. *B:* I **did** too.
*A:* Did it rain yesterday? *B:* No, it **didn't**.

lesson.text: After *Yes* or *No* use the full verb: *Yes, I am*, not ~~Yes, I'm~~.

exercises.explanation: we + past of be = we were (we were hungry).

exercises.prompt: I'm not married, but my brother ___ .
exercises.explanation: my brother = he, so we say is (he is married).

exercises.prompt: Match each sentence with the verb that finishes it.

pairs.left: I haven't seen the film, but Tom
Karen won't be here, but Chris
Bill can't help you, but I
I don't like hot weather, but Sue

exercises.explanation: You cannot end with the short form 's. Say: but he is.

exercises.prompt: I was working, but my friends ___ .
exercises.explanation: my friends = they, so the negative is weren't.

exercises.prompt: I'm ready to go, but Tom ___ .
exercises.explanation: Tom = he, so the negative is isn't.

exercises.prompt: Which verb finishes each sentence: do, does or did?

items.text: *A:* Do you enjoy your work? *B:* Yes, I ___ .
You don't know Paul very well, but I ___ .
I don't watch TV much, but Peter ___ .
My mother wears glasses, and my father ___ too.
I didn't enjoy the party, but my friends ___ .
*A:* Did it rain yesterday? *B:* Yes, it ___ .

exercises.prompt: Steve is happy today, but he ___ yesterday.
exercises.explanation: yesterday = past, so we use the past negative wasn't.

exercises.prompt: I haven't got a telescope, but I know somebody who ___ .
exercises.explanation: somebody = he/she, so we say has (has got a telescope).

exercises.prompt: I would like to help you, but I'm afraid I ___ .
exercises.explanation: I can't = I can't help you.
Yes, I am. After Yes we use the full form am, not I'm.

exercises.explanation: she will = she will pass her driving test.
